es: Analizar un cartel ajeno, crear un eslogan con una técnica de persuasión y presentar una campaña vecinal con pregunta retórica, énfasis, una objeción admitida y una llamada a la acción concreta.

teaching.en: The headline of the poster uses contrast, noisy streets against quiet minds, and this clash is designed to catch the eye of every passer-by.
teaching.es: El titular del cartel usa el contraste, calles ruidosas frente a mentes tranquilas, y este choque está diseñado para llamar la atención de cualquier transeúnte.
teaching.explanationEs: Analiza el titular: nombra la técnica y explica su efecto (to catch the eye).
segments: The headline of the poster uses contrast, noisy streets against quiet minds,
and this clash is designed to catch the eye of every passer-by.
teaching.audioText: The headline of the poster uses contrast, noisy streets against quiet minds, and this clash is designed to catch the eye of every passer-by.

teaching.en: Our campaign aims to plant thirty trees in the neighbourhood and to raise awareness of how much shade and clean air a single tree can give.
teaching.es: Nuestra campaña pretende plantar treinta árboles en el barrio y sensibilizar sobre la sombra y el aire limpio que puede dar un solo árbol.
teaching.explanationEs: Aim to + verbo: el objetivo; raise awareness of + nombre: sensibilizar sobre algo.
segments: Our campaign aims to plant thirty trees in the neighbourhood and to raise
awareness of how much shade and clean air a single tree can give.
teaching.audioText: Our campaign aims to plant thirty trees in the neighbourhood and to raise awareness of how much shade and clean air a single tree can give.

teaching.en: The picture of a child beside a busy road makes the poster appeal to parents, who are the target audience of this campaign.
teaching.es: La imagen de un niño junto a una carretera concurrida hace que el cartel apele a los padres, que son el público objetivo de esta campaña.
teaching.explanationEs: Una imagen también persuade; target audience = las personas a las que va dirigido el mensaje.
segments: The picture of a child beside a busy road makes the poster
appeal to parents, who are the target audience of this campaign.
teaching.audioText: The picture of a child beside a busy road makes the poster appeal to parents, who are the target audience of this campaign.

teaching.en: In my pitch, I will open with a rhetorical question, use a tricolon in the middle and close with a call to action.
teaching.es: En mi presentación abriré con una pregunta retórica, usaré un tricolon en el medio y cerraré con una llamada a la acción.
teaching.explanationEs: Un pitch breve tiene apertura, desarrollo y cierre.
segments: In my pitch, I will open with a rhetorical question, use a
tricolon in the middle and close with a call to action.
teaching.audioText: In my pitch, I will open with a rhetorical question, use a tricolon in the middle and close with a call to action.

teaching.en: Every volunteer will sign a pledge to bring three neighbours to the park on Saturday, which is how a campaign can spread the word.
teaching.es: Cada voluntario firmará un compromiso de llevar a tres vecinos al parque el sábado, y así puede una campaña correr la voz.
teaching.explanationEs: Pledge = compromiso firmado; spread the word = difundir el mensaje de persona a persona.
segments: Every volunteer will sign a pledge to bring three neighbours to the
park on Saturday, which is how a campaign can spread the word.
teaching.audioText: Every volunteer will sign a pledge to bring three neighbours to the park on Saturday, which is how a campaign can spread the word.

teaching.en: A strong call to action is concrete: it tells each volunteer who should come, where to meet and when, instead of asking for vague support.
teaching.es: Una buena llamada a la acción es concreta: dice a cada voluntario quién debe venir, dónde reunirse y cuándo, en lugar de pedir un apoyo vago.
teaching.explanationEs: Concreto = quién, dónde y cuándo; vague support no mueve a nadie.

come, where to meet and when, instead of asking for vague support.

prompt.es: Elige el análisis correcto del titular del cartel.

choices.text: The headline uses repetition to catch the eye.
The headline uses contrast to catch the eye.
The headline asks a rhetorical question to catch the eye.

feedback.es: Empty y full se oponen: es un contraste; no hay palabra repetida ni pregunta.

hint.es: Busca dos ideas opuestas en el titular.

origin.text: A charity poster for a community garden shows a cracked, empty car park beside a bed of flowers, under the headline: Empty lots, full hearts.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nuestra campaña quiere mejorar el barrio.»

feedback.es: El objetivo de la campaña se expresa con to + verbo.

hint.es: Aquí va el infinitivo con to, no for.

origin.text: Our campaign is ___ improve the neighbourhood. We are not asking for money; we are asking for a few hours of work on Saturday.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada voluntario firmará un compromiso antes de irse.»

answer.text: Every volunteer will sign a pledge before leaving

feedback.es: La llamada a la acción es concreta: cada voluntario y lo que debe hacer.

prompt.es: Elige el eslogan que usa un tricolon correcto.

choices.text: Clean parks, safe streets, we are happy neighbours.
Clean parks, safe streets and neighbours happy.
Clean parks, safe streets, happy neighbours.

feedback.es: El tricolon mantiene la misma forma (adjetivo + nombre plural) en las tres partes.

origin.text: The committee must choose one slogan for the campaign banner, and the winning line has to list three things in exactly the same way.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada parte de la campaña con su función.

pairs: Would you let your child play here?
It is such a clean park that visitors smile.
Join us on Saturday at nine.
We will raise awareness of the problem.

feedback.es: La pregunta abre, such da énfasis, la invitación concreta cierra el pitch y el objetivo dice para qué sirve la campaña.

prompt.es: Escucha el pitch y elige la llamada a la acción.

choices.text: Go to the park on Saturday and sign the pledge.
Write to the newspaper on Saturday at ten.
Call the council office on Monday morning.

feedback.es: El pitch termina pidiendo ir al parque el sábado a las diez y firmar el compromiso: quién, dónde y cuándo.

origin.audio: Good evening, neighbours. Why should our children cross a busy road every day just to reach the park? This neighbourhood needs a safe crossing, and it needs it now. The traffic here is so heavy that some parents no longer let their children walk to school. I know that the council has little money, and I accept that. But a crossing costs far less than an accident. So on Saturday at ten, come to the park, sign the pledge and bring one neighbour with you.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué admite la oradora que hay poco dinero.

choices.text: To ask the audience to give money to the council.
To sound fair before arguing that the cost is justified.
To suggest that the crossing is not necessary.

feedback.es: Reconoce la objeción (I accept that) y enseguida la rebate (a crossing costs far less than an accident): concede un punto para ganar credibilidad.

origin.text: The designer put a picture of a child beside an empty playground, and the image is meant to ___ the eye of every parent who walks past the poster.

prompt.es: Analiza el cartel y presenta tu campaña (110-280 palabras).

answer.text: The poster uses contrast in its headline, loud streets and quiet children, to catch the eye, and the picture of a child makes parents feel worried. Our slogan is: safe streets, happy children, stronger neighbourhoods. Our campaign is to build a safe crossing near the school. Why should our children cross such a busy road every day? The traffic is so heavy that parents are afraid to let them walk. I know that the council has little money, and I accept that, but a crossing costs far less than an accident. Every volunteer can help: join us on Saturday at ten at the park, bring a friend and sign the petition. Together we can raise awareness and make our neighbourhood safer. Who would refuse to give one hour to protect a child?

Every volunteer can help: join us on Saturday at ten at the park, bring a friend and sign the petition. Together we can raise awareness and make our neighbourhood safer. Who would refuse to give one hour to protect a child?

The headline of this poster uses contrast to catch the eye of parents: loud streets against quiet children. The picture also appeals to their feelings. Our slogan is: fewer cars, cleaner air, safer children. Our campaign is to build a safe crossing near the school. Who wants to see a child cross such a dangerous road? The traffic is so heavy that nobody feels safe. The council may say that it has no money, and that is a fair point, but a crossing is cheaper than an accident. Please join us on Saturday at ten at the park, every volunteer is welcome, and sign the petition before you leave. Together we can make this neighbourhood a place where children are safe.

feedback.es: Un caso completo analiza el cartel, propone un eslogan con técnica y cierra con una presentación persuasiva y una petición concreta.

origin.text: Caso: un cartel del barrio con el titular «Loud streets, quiet children» y la imagen de un niño junto a una calle con mucho tráfico. Escribe en inglés (170–220 palabras): 1) la técnica del cartel y su efecto; 2) un eslogan propio con una técnica; 3) un pitch breve con pregunta retórica, so o such, una objeción que admites y una llamada a la acción concreta (quién, dónde y cuándo).

prompt.es: Elige qué actitud deja entrever el autor de la carta ante la campaña.

choices.text: Total enthusiasm for every decision made.
Anger at the volunteers for wasting time.
Respect for the effort, with a polite complaint.

feedback.es: Elogia el trabajo de los voluntarios, pero señala con cortesía que nadie consultó a los vecinos ni eligió el color: respeto con una queja educada.

origin.text: I respect the volunteers who cleaned the park last Sunday, and I am sure they worked hard. However, I notice that the benches were painted a colour nobody chose, and that nobody asked the people who live opposite the park.

origin.text: Every week another family writes to the council to complain. It is ___ a serious problem that we must act today.
